scope: Bounded proof audit under the user-accepted manuscript inputs

steps: The proof text is usable and is read in its displayed order.
The strict genuine barrier is an accepted input, not inferred merely from an ambiguous definition of bigness.
ddc u is closed even if theta is nonclosed; theta-psh bounded u gives ddc u>=-theta.
Compactness allows uniform Hermitian curvature constants and normalization of the upper bounds of u and rho.
U is arbitrary subject to local boundedness of rho; no analytic or canonical description of U is required.

statement_checks.location: The general curvature modulus — classical input
steps: Use Demailly's notation psi=u, alpha_D=0, T=ddc u, gamma=-theta; gamma is only required to have continuous real coefficients, whereas closedness is required of T and alpha_D.
Because theta is smooth, ddc u>=-theta makes u locally the sum of a psh function and a smooth function, as required by the source.
Take the source's auxiliary curvature form B=A omega with A>=0 large: compactness bounds the negative Chern bisectional curvature, so in particular the required bound on orthogonal pairs holds.
The source's equations (3.1)-(3.2) use the same positive normalized radial formal-exph averaging. They are smooth in (z,w) for w nonzero; no continuity of u is required.
Theorem 4.1 provides the full Hessian estimate, not merely a base Hessian estimate. Numerical ddc normalization factors are absorbed in fixed constants.

The source states lambda=t partial_t(R_t u+K0 t^2) is nonnegative and increasing; its proof gives logarithmic convexity. Monotone convergence to the genuine quasi-psh representative yields R_t u+K0 t^2>=u pointwise.
The source's error function tends to zero; no linear or power rate is assumed. Exact reference confirmation is recorded separately.

statement_checks.location: Lemma general-kiselman-modulus — H and logarithmic convexity
steps: Set H=R_t u+K t^2+K t for K>=K0 with K>0, as allowed by 'sufficiently large'.
Its logarithmic derivative is tilde-lambda=lambda+2(K-K0)t^2+Kt>=lambda.

Its second logarithmic derivative is partial_logt lambda+4(K-K0)t^2+Kt>0. Hence H is strictly logarithmically convex and increasing. This uses the actual source assertion about lambda, not an inference from monotonicity alone.

statement_checks.location: Lemma general-kiselman-modulus — mixed and vertical error absorption
steps: For w nonzero, partial_w partial_barw |w|=1/(4|w|); the dd^c factor only changes fixed constants.
The term K|w| therefore supplies a positive vertical coefficient comparable to K/t. K|w|^2 supplies another nonnegative vertical coefficient.
Young's inequality bounds C|zeta||eta| by C't|zeta|^2+K|eta|^2/(8t), where C' is fixed once K is fixed.
For all sufficiently small t, the remaining positive vertical coefficient absorbs the fixed C|eta|^2 error as well.
The remaining negative base form is -theta-(A lambda+epsilon0(t)+C't)omega.
Since A>=0 and tilde-lambda>=lambda, replacing lambda by tilde-lambda weakens this lower bound in the valid direction.

An increasing nonnegative majorant epsilon(t) of epsilon0(t)+C't tends to zero and is independent of c and delta. This is the absorption mechanism of Remark 4.7, with the explicitly justified larger correction used in this proof.

statement_checks.location: Lemma general-kiselman-modulus — boundedness and minimizing radii
steps: Positivity and normalization of R_t give inf_X u<=R_t u<=sup_X u, uniformly in z and t.
For fixed c>0 and delta>0, the expression tends uniformly to +infinity as t decreases to zero. Thus all minimizers lie in one compact interval [b,delta] with b>0.
The objective is smooth for t>0, continuous in (z,t), and strictly convex in log t after subtracting the linear logarithmic term. It therefore has exactly one minimizing radius.
The interior stationarity condition is tilde-lambda=c. At t=delta the left derivative of the convex objective is <=0, so tilde-lambda<=c; the boundary sign is correct.
The minimum value is finite and continuous in z by minimization over the fixed compact interval. The unique minimizer is continuous by the same compactness argument, without assuming continuity of u.
The estimate R_t u+Kt^2>=u gives Phi>=u-K(delta^2+delta), since Kt>=0 and -c log(t/delta)>=0. Evaluation at t=delta gives Phi<=R_delta u. In particular Phi is bounded.

statement_checks.location: Lemma general-kiselman-modulus — localization and capped minimum
steps: Fix z0 and a>0. If t*(z0)<delta, choose an upper radius r+ with t*(z0)<r+<delta and tilde-lambda(z0,r+)<c+a, using continuity and tilde-lambda(z0,t*)=c.
After shrinking to a coordinate ball V around z0, continuity of t* keeps every nearby minimizer below r+, and continuity of tilde-lambda preserves its bound at r+.
If t*(z0)=delta, keep r+=delta. The inequality tilde-lambda(z0,delta)<=c and continuity ensure tilde-lambda(z,delta)<c+a on a smaller V.
In either case choose a fixed lower radius r->0 below all nearby minimizers. Monotonicity of tilde-lambda bounds it by c+a on the whole radial interval (r-,r+).

When a minimizing radius equals the cap, continuity at t=delta shows that the infimum over t<delta equals the closed-cap minimum. Kiselman's principle does not require attainment in the open interval.
The logarithmic substitution w=exp(tau) gives the product V times the strip log r-<Re tau<log r+, which is pseudoconvex after taking V to be a ball and has connected convex real fibers.
Radial invariance gives independence of Im tau. The penalty -c Re tau is pluriharmonic on the strip and does not alter the Hessian inequality.

statement_checks.location: Lemma general-kiselman-modulus — smooth-form freezing and current bound
steps: On the localized product the full Hessian of the objective is bounded below by -B(z), where B(z)=theta(z)+(A(c+a)+epsilon(delta))omega(z).
No local potential for nonclosed theta is assumed. In a chart, freeze B at z0 and choose a real quadratic q with dd^c q=B(z0)+h beta, where beta is the Euclidean positive form and h>0.
Continuity of the coefficients and shrinking V ensure B(z)<=B(z0)+h beta. Hence the corrected objective is genuinely plurisubharmonic on the whole product.
The allowed Kiselman principle gives that Phi+q is psh on V; the fiber infimum is finite and continuous, so no representative ambiguity arises.

The resulting inequality dd^c Phi>=-B(z0)-h beta implies dd^c Phi>=-B(z)-2h beta on a further shrink. Covering by these neighborhoods, converting beta to a uniform local multiple of omega, and letting h decrease to zero gives the desired continuous-form current inequality for fixed a.
Letting a decrease to zero gives theta+dd^c Phi>=-(Ac+epsilon(delta))omega. The local psh correction also proves quasi-plurisubharmonicity.
Finally R_t u+Kt^2=(R_t u+K0t^2)+(K-K0)t^2 remains increasing in t and tends pointwise to u.
The curvature-modulus estimate has not changed the averaging operator.
Boundedness of u and R_t u-u>=-Kt^2 are exactly the accepted smoothing73 hypotheses.
Therefore the accepted adjoint-cancellation argument gives ||R_t u-u||_L1(dV)<=Ct^2 and ||grad R_t u||_infinity<=C/t.
No estimate for epsilon(t) is used to derive these two bounds, and no prior continuity of u is used.
Adding constants leaves ddc u and its Monge–Ampere measure unchanged, so u can be normalized to [-C0,0].
A genuine quasi-psh rho has finite supremum on compact X; subtracting a constant gives rho<=-C0-1 without changing strictness.
The allowed stability range is nonempty for p>1. For n>=1, (p-1)/(np+p-1)<1/2, so choosing eta in this range gives 0<alpha=2eta<1.
Set c=delta^alpha+epsilon(delta)>0; then c tends to zero and epsilon(delta)<=c.
With e=Ac+epsilon(delta), s=e/kappa is nonnegative, tends to zero, satisfies s kappa=e, and obeys s<=(A+1)c/kappa.
statement_checks.persistence_note: Retry of the original sequential record after a permission-review timeout; sequence reflects verification order.

statement_checks.location: Theorem local-big-bounded-continuity — barrier correction and ordering
steps: The affine-current identity is theta+dd^c v=[theta+dd^c Phi+s(theta+dd^c rho)]/(1+s).
Its numerator is bounded below by (-e+s kappa)omega=0; the identity works for nonclosed theta.
Phi is bounded quasi-psh and rho is genuine theta-psh, so the affine combination is a genuine theta-psh function, possibly unbounded below.
For delta sufficiently small K(delta^2+delta)<=1. The lemma's lower bound gives Phi>=u-1>=-C0-1>=rho.
At the cap Phi<=R_delta u, and positivity of the normalized average gives R_delta u<=0.
Since rho<=Phi and s>=0, v<=Phi<=R_delta u<=0. No boundedness below of v is asserted or required.
The target u is bounded in the accepted interval, solves MA_theta(u)=f dV with f nonnegative in Lp, and the comparison v is theta-psh and <=0.
The accepted stability71 expressly permits this possibly unbounded comparison potential and has a constant independent of it.
Pointwise (v-u)_+ <= (R_delta u-u)_+ <= |R_delta u-u|, including points where v=-infinity.
Consequently its integral is at most C delta^2 and stability gives sup_X(v-u)_+<=C delta^(2eta)=C delta^alpha, uniformly in delta.

statement_checks.location: Theorem local-big-bounded-continuity — local bound for Phi-u
steps: At rho>=-M all terms in Phi-u=(1+s)(v-u)+s(u-rho) are finite.
The equality follows by multiplying the definition of v by 1+s and subtracting u; its sign is correct.
Here v-u<=C delta^alpha, u<=0 implies u-rho<=M, and 1+s is bounded for small delta.
Thus Phi-u<=C delta^alpha+C_M s<=C_M c. The constant is uniform on {rho>=-M} for fixed M.

statement_checks.location: Theorem local-big-bounded-continuity — lower bound for minimizing radius
steps: At the minimizing t, solve the defining identity for -c log(t/delta).
Using R_t u+Kt^2>=u and Kt>=0 gives -c log(t/delta)<=Phi-u+K(delta^2+delta).
For 0<delta<1 and alpha<1, delta^2+delta<=2 delta^alpha<=2c; hence the right side is <=C_M c.
Divide by positive c to obtain log(delta/t)<=C_M and t>=a_M delta with a_M=exp(-C_M)>0, decreased to at most 1 if necessary.
The constant a_M is independent of delta and the base point in {rho>=-M}; no power rate for epsilon is needed.
Since a_M delta<=t, monotonicity gives R_(a_M delta)u+K(a_M delta)^2<=R_t u+Kt^2.
Rearranging the minimum identity gives R_t u+Kt^2=Phi+Kdelta^2+Kdelta-Kt+c log(t/delta)<=Phi+Kdelta^2+Kdelta.
Combine with Phi-u<=C_M c and delta<=c to get R_(a_M delta)u-u<=C_M c.
The monotone lower estimate gives R_(a_M delta)u-u>=-K(a_M delta)^2, also controlled by c.
Together these prove the displayed uniform absolute error bound C_M(delta^alpha+epsilon(delta)) on {rho>=-M}, tending to zero.
Every compact subset of U has a uniform lower bound for rho by a finite cover from its local boundedness.
Choose that fixed M and a_M. A sequence delta_j decreasing to zero gives smooth functions R_(a_M delta_j)u converging uniformly to u on the compact subset.
Applying this to compact neighborhoods contained in U proves continuity at every point of U. No continuity across the complement of U is inferred.

statement_checks.location: Closing paragraph — continuity modulus and scope
steps: For a compact K subset U, the uniform error bound and global gradient bound give |u(x)-u(y)|<=2C_M(delta^alpha+epsilon(delta))+C d_omega(x,y)/(a_M delta) for x,y in K.
Taking delta comparable to the square root of d_omega(x,y), for instance, makes both terms tend to zero and yields a modulus with no assumed power bound on epsilon.
The proof does not claim a Holder exponent from an unspecified epsilon. Its statement that a Holder conclusion by this argument needs a proved power control is appropriately limited to this argument.
Boundedness of u was used in the smoothing input, uniform exclusion of t=0, normalization, and accepted stability; the argument does not establish regularity for unbounded solutions.
The barrier lower bound was used only on fixed sublevel sets {rho>=-M}; the proof does not establish continuity at its poles.
Compactness supplies uniform regularization constants, finite suprema for normalization, and the global setting of the accepted stability input.
Hermitian omega is only a regularization metric and a comparison form for strictness.
Theta smoothness supplies a continuous lower bound for Demailly and permits freezing; closedness of theta is never needed.

Theta semipositivity and the stated big setting are inherited in the accepted manuscript inputs. Once the genuine strict rho is explicitly assumed, no further numerical use of bigness is needed; this redundancy is harmless, not an omitted existence argument.
The strict positive kappa is used exactly in s kappa=e. Local boundedness of rho is used exactly for compact-set uniform convergence.
The Lp hypothesis, p>1, and equation for u enter the accepted one-sided stability estimate and the admissible eta. The smoothing argument uses the accepted positive smooth measure dV.
Connectedness is part of the accepted compact setting and is not separately needed in the elementary local argument; no contradiction follows from this harmless redundancy.
No BMP/PVP assumption, KN19 substitution, uniform convergence deduced from Dini before continuity, unproved power modulus, or prior continuity of u has been introduced.

reference_checks.referenced_statement: Kiselman minimum principle (partial Legendre transformation): If V is a complex domain, I is an open interval in R, and F is plurisubharmonic on V times {tau in C: Re tau in I} and independent of Im tau, then the function z -> inf_{s in I} F(z,s) is plurisubharmonic or identically minus infinity. Equivalently, for a rotation-invariant plurisubharmonic function on V times an annulus with logarithmically convex radial interval, its fiberwise infimum is plurisubharmonic. Apply with a finite locally bounded infimum after a smooth base quadratic correction.
reference_checks.arxiv_comparison: Arxiv search returned a more restrictive smooth subequation proposition requiring an interior attained minimum (1806.06033, Proposition 8.5), as well as unrelated results. That restricted proposition was not used in the capped case.
reference_checks.source_location: Deng–Wang–Zhang–Zhou, A new proof of Kiselman's minimum principle for plurisubharmonic functions, Theorems 1.1–1.2, p.1; a primary proof of the accepted principle.
reference_checks.context_expansion: The tube formulation assumes a pseudoconvex total domain with connected tube fibers and a psh function independent of imaginary fiber coordinates. The rotation-invariant formulation uses connected Reinhardt fibers. Neither formulation requires the fiber infimum to be attained.
exact_specialization: After logarithmic lifting, the domain is a coordinate ball times an open strip, hence pseudoconvex with connected fibers; the corrected objective is independent of the imaginary fiber coordinate.
The Hessian after the explicitly described quadratic freezing correction is nonnegative in all base–fiber directions.

For an upper-cap minimizer, the infimum over the open interval approaching delta equals the capped value by continuity. Therefore the lack of interior attainment in this case violates no hypothesis of the accepted principle.
The infimum is bounded and continuous, so it is the correct psh representative after the quadratic correction. Taking arbitrarily small freezing and a-errors yields the stated current inequality.

results.title: A generalization of Nadel vanishing theorem
results.theorem:
Let $(X,\omega)$ be a complex manifold equipped with a Hermitian metric $\omega$, and $\Omega\Subset X$ be an open subset.
Assume that $T=\widetilde{T}+\frac{\mathrm{i}}{\pi}\partial\bar{\partial}\varphi$
is a closed $(1,1)$-current on $X$,
where $\widetilde{T}$ is a smooth real $(1,1)$-form and $\varphi$ is a quasi-plurisubharmonic function.
Let $\gamma$ be a continuous real $(1,1)$-form such that $T\geqslant\gamma$. Suppose that the Chern curvature tensor of $TX$ satisfies



$\left(\mathrm{i}\Theta_{T_{X}}+\theta\otimes\mathrm{Id}_{T_{X}}\right)\left(\kappa_{1}\otimes\kappa_{2},\kappa_{1}\otimes\kappa_{2}\right)\geqslant 0\quad\forall\kappa_{1},\kappa_{2}\in T_{X}~{}\text{with}~{}\langle\kappa_{1},\kappa_{2}\rangle=0$



for some continuous nonnegative $(1,1)$-form $\theta$ on $X$.
Then there is a family of closed $(1,1)$-currents $T_{\varsigma,\varepsilon}=\widetilde{T}+\frac{\mathrm{i}}{\pi}\partial\bar{\partial}\varphi_{\varsigma,\varepsilon}$ on $X$ such that


(i)

$\varphi_{\varsigma,\varepsilon}$ is quasi-plurisubharmonic on a neighborhood of $\bar{\Omega}$, smooth on $X\backslash E_{\sigma}(T)$, increasing with respect to $\varsigma$ and $\varepsilon$ on $\Omega$, and converges to $\varphi$ on $\Omega$ as $\varepsilon\to 0$,



(ii)

$T_{\varsigma,\varepsilon}\geqslant\gamma-\varsigma\theta-\delta_{\varepsilon}\omega$ on $\Omega$,



where $E_{\varsigma}(T)=\left\{x\in X;\nu(T,x)\geqslant\varsigma\right\}$, $\varsigma>0$, is the $\varsigma$-upperlevel set of Lelong numbers, and $\{\delta_{\varepsilon}\}$ is an increasing family of positive numbers such that $\lim_{\varepsilon\to 0}\delta_{\varepsilon}=0$.

results.title: Optimal $L^2$ extension of sections from subvarieties in weakly pseudoconvex manifolds
results.theorem:
Let $(X,\omega)$ be a complex manifold equipped with a Hermitian
metric $\omega$, and Ω⊂⊂X\Omega\subset\subset X be an open subset.
Assume that $T=\widetilde{T}+\frac{\sqrt{-1}}{\pi}\partial\bar{\partial}\varphi$ is a closed $(1,1)$-current on $X$,
where $\widetilde{T}$ is a smooth real $(1,1)$-form and $\varphi$ is
a quasi-plurisubharmonic function. Let $\gamma$ be a continuous real
$(1,1)$-form such that $T\geq\gamma$. Suppose that the Chern
curvature tensor of $T_{X}$ satisfies



$(\sqrt{-1}\Theta_{T_{X}}+\varpi\otimes\mathrm{Id}_{T_{X}})(\kappa_{1}\otimes\kappa_{2},\kappa_{1}\otimes\kappa_{2})\geq 0\quad(\forall\kappa_{1},\kappa_{2}\in T_{X}\text{ with }\langle\kappa_{1},\kappa_{2}\rangle=0)$



for some continuous nonnegative
$(1,1)$-form $\varpi$ on $X$. Then there is a family of closed
$(1,1)$-currents $T_{\varsigma,\rho}=\widetilde{T}+\frac{\sqrt{-1}}{\pi}\partial\bar{\partial}\varphi_{\varsigma,\rho}$ defined
on a neighborhood of $\overline{\Omega}$ ($\varsigma\in(0,+\infty)$ and $\rho\in(0,\rho_{1})$ for some
positive number $\rho_{1}$) independent of $\gamma$, such that


$(i)$

$\varphi_{\varsigma,\rho}$ is quasi-plurisubharmonic on a neighborhood of $\overline{\Omega}$,
smooth on $\Omega\setminus E_{\varsigma}(T)$, increasing with respect to
$\varsigma$ and $\rho$ on $\Omega$, and converges to $\varphi$ on
$\Omega$ as $\rho\rightarrow 0$,



$(ii)$

$T_{\varsigma,\rho}\geq\gamma-\varsigma\varpi-\delta_{\rho}\omega$ on $\Omega$,



where $E_{\varsigma}(T):=\{x\in X:\,\nu(T,x)\geq\varsigma\}$
$(\varsigma>0)$ is the $\varsigma$-upperlevel set of Lelong numbers,
and $\{\delta_{\rho}\}$ is an increasing family of positive numbers
such that $\lim\limits_{\rho\rightarrow 0}\delta_{\rho}=0$.

results.title: Metrics with cone singularities along normal crossing divisors and holomorphic tensor fields
results.theorem:
Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold and $D=\sum(1-\tau_{j})Y_{j}$ a divisor with simple normal crossings such that its coefficients satisfy $0<\tau_{j}\leqslant 1/2$. Let $\mu_{D}=dV/\prod_{j}|s_{j}|^{2(1-\tau_{j})}$ be a volume form with cone singularities along $D$, $\psi$ a bounded quasi-psh function, and $\omega$ a Kähler form on $X$. Then any (bounded) solution $\varphi$ of



$(\omega+dd^{c}\varphi)^{n}=e^{-\psi}\mu_{D}$



is Hölder-continuous and the metric $\omega+dd^{c}\varphi$ has cone singularities along $D$.

results.title: Plurisubharmonic functions and positive currents of type (1,1) over almost complex manifolds
results.theorem:
(Demailly)
Soit $(X,J,\omega)$ une variété complexe hermitienne telle que

$G^{\perp_{\alpha}}_{\omega}(T_{X,J})\geq 0$
pour une certaine $\alpha$ et soit $\psi$ une fonction quasi-plurisousharmonique telle que $i\partial_{{}_{J}}\bar{\partial}_{{}_{J}}\psi\geq\gamma$, où $\gamma$ est une $(1,1)$-forme continue. Soit $\operatorname{exph}^{\omega}$ la partie holomorphe sur les fibres du fibré tangent de l’application exponentielle $\operatorname{exp}^{\omega}$.
L’opérateur régularisant



$\psi_{\varepsilon}(x):=\int\limits_{\zeta\in T_{X,x}}\psi\circ\operatorname{exph}^{\omega}_{x}\,(\zeta)\cdot\chi_{\varepsilon}(|\zeta|^{2}_{\omega_{x}})\frac{\omega^{n}_{x,\zeta}}{n!}$



vérifie les propriétées suivantes:

A) la suite de fonctions $(\psi_{\varepsilon})_{\varepsilon>0}\subset{\cal E}(X,\mathbb{R})$ converge ponctuellement de façon décroissante vers $\psi$ lorsque $\varepsilon>0$ tend vers zéro,

B) on a le contrôle
$i\partial_{{}_{J}}\bar{\partial}_{{}_{J}}\psi_{\varepsilon}\geq\gamma-\delta_{\varepsilon}\omega$ sur la perte de positivité, où $(\delta_{\varepsilon})_{\varepsilon>0}\subset(0,+\infty)$ est une famille de
réels qui tend vers zéro de façon décroissante lorsque $\varepsilon>0$ tend vers zéro.

on a neighborhood of $\overline{\Omega}$, for some continuous nonnegative
$(1,1)$-form $\varpi$ on $X$. Assume that $\varphi$ is a quasi-psh function on $X$, and let $\gamma$ be a continuous real
$(1,1)$-form such that $\sqrt{-1}\partial\bar{\partial}\varphi\geq\gamma$ in the sense of currents. Then there is a family of functions $\varphi_{\varsigma,\rho}$ defined
on a neighborhood of $\overline{\Omega}$ ($\varsigma\in(0,+\infty)$ and $\rho\in(0,\rho_{1})$ for some
positive number $\rho_{1}$) independent of $\gamma$, such that


$(i)$

$\varphi_{\varsigma,\rho}$ is quasi-psh on a neighborhood of $\overline{\Omega}$,
smooth on $\overline{\Omega}\setminus E_{\varsigma}(\varphi)$, increasing with respect to
$\varsigma$ and $\rho$ on $\overline{\Omega}$, and converges to $\varphi$ on
$\overline{\Omega}$ as $\rho\rightarrow 0$,



$(ii)$

$\sqrt{-1}\partial\bar{\partial}\varphi_{\varsigma,\rho}\geq\gamma-\pi\varsigma\varpi-\delta_{\rho}\omega$ on $\Omega$,



where $E_{\varsigma}(\varphi):=\{x\in X:\,\nu(\varphi,x)\geq\varsigma\}$
$(\varsigma>0)$ is the $\varsigma$-upperlevel set of Lelong numbers,
and $\{\delta_{\rho}\}$ is an increasing family of positive numbers
such that $\lim\limits_{\rho\rightarrow 0}\delta_{\rho}=0$.

remark.query: Demailly 1994 Remark 4.7, Regularization of closed positive currents of type (1,1) by the flow of a Chern connection: Set Psi-tilde(x,w)=Psi(x,w)+|w|. Its logarithmic derivative lambda-tilde=lambda+|w|-2K|w|^2 is positive and increasing for small |w|. Adding |w| supplies the vertical Hessian |eta|^2/(4|w|); absorb K|zeta||eta| <= 2K^2|w||zeta|^2+|eta|^2/(8|w|). The resulting full Hessian is bounded below by gamma-lambda-tilde B-delta-tilde(|w|) omega in the base directions only, with delta-tilde(t) tending to zero.

results.title: Plurisubharmonic functions and positive currents of type (1,1) over almost complex manifolds
results.theorem:
(Demailly)
Soit $(X,J,\omega)$ une variété complexe hermitienne telle que

$G^{\perp_{\alpha}}_{\omega}(T_{X,J})\geq 0$
pour une certaine $\alpha$ et soit $\psi$ une fonction quasi-plurisousharmonique telle que $i\partial_{{}_{J}}\bar{\partial}_{{}_{J}}\psi\geq\gamma$, où $\gamma$ est une $(1,1)$-forme continue. Soit $\operatorname{exph}^{\omega}$ la partie holomorphe sur les fibres du fibré tangent de l’application exponentielle $\operatorname{exp}^{\omega}$.
L’opérateur régularisant



$\psi_{\varepsilon}(x):=\int\limits_{\zeta\in T_{X,x}}\psi\circ\operatorname{exph}^{\omega}_{x}\,(\zeta)\cdot\chi_{\varepsilon}(|\zeta|^{2}_{\omega_{x}})\frac{\omega^{n}_{x,\zeta}}{n!}$



vérifie les propriétées suivantes:

A) la suite de fonctions $(\psi_{\varepsilon})_{\varepsilon>0}\subset{\cal E}(X,\mathbb{R})$ converge ponctuellement de façon décroissante vers $\psi$ lorsque $\varepsilon>0$ tend vers zéro,

B) on a le contrôle
$i\partial_{{}_{J}}\bar{\partial}_{{}_{J}}\psi_{\varepsilon}\geq\gamma-\delta_{\varepsilon}\omega$ sur la perte de positivité, où $(\delta_{\varepsilon})_{\varepsilon>0}\subset(0,+\infty)$ est une famille de
réels qui tend vers zéro de façon décroissante lorsque $\varepsilon>0$ tend vers zéro.

results.title: Extension of cohomology classes and holomorphic sections defined on subvarieties
results.theorem:
Let $X$ be a complex manifold equipped with a Hermitian
metric $\omega$, and Ω⊂⊂X\Omega\subset\subset X be an open subset. Suppose that the Chern
curvature tensor of $T_{X}$ satisfies



$\bigg{(}\frac{\sqrt{-1}}{2\pi}\Theta_{T_{X}}+\varpi\otimes\mathrm{Id}_{T_{X}}\bigg{)}(\kappa_{1}\otimes\kappa_{2},\kappa_{1}\otimes\kappa_{2})\geq 0\quad(\forall\kappa_{1},\kappa_{2}\in T_{X}\text{ with }\langle\kappa_{1},\kappa_{2}\rangle=0)$



on a neighborhood of $\overline{\Omega}$, for some continuous nonnegative
$(1,1)$-form $\varpi$ on $X$. Assume that $\varphi$ is a quasi-psh function on $X$, and let $\gamma$ be a continuous real
$(1,1)$-form such that $\sqrt{-1}\partial\bar{\partial}\varphi\geq\gamma$ in the sense of currents. Then there is a family of functions $\varphi_{\varsigma,\rho}$ defined
on a neighborhood of $\overline{\Omega}$ ($\varsigma\in(0,+\infty)$ and $\rho\in(0,\rho_{1})$ for some
positive number $\rho_{1}$) independent of $\gamma$, such that


$(i)$

$\varphi_{\varsigma,\rho}$ is quasi-psh on a neighborhood of $\overline{\Omega}$,
smooth on $\overline{\Omega}\setminus E_{\varsigma}(\varphi)$, increasing with respect to
$\varsigma$ and $\rho$ on $\overline{\Omega}$, and converges to $\varphi$ on
$\overline{\Omega}$ as $\rho\rightarrow 0$,



$(ii)$

$\sqrt{-1}\partial\bar{\partial}\varphi_{\varsigma,\rho}\geq\gamma-\pi\varsigma\varpi-\delta_{\rho}\omega$ on $\Omega$,



where $E_{\varsigma}(\varphi):=\{x\in X:\,\nu(\varphi,x)\geq\varsigma\}$
$(\varsigma>0)$ is the $\varsigma$-upperlevel set of Lelong numbers,
and $\{\delta_{\rho}\}$ is an increasing family of positive numbers
such that $\lim\limits_{\rho\rightarrow 0}\delta_{\rho}=0$.

results.title: Lelong-Skoda transform for compact Kaehler manifolds and self-intersection inequalities
results.theorem:
Let $S$ be a positive closed current of bidegree $(1,1)$ on a compact Kähler manifold $X$. Let $\varphi$ be a quasi-psh function such that $S=\alpha+dd^{c}\varphi$ where $\alpha$ is a smooth $(1,1)$ form. Then for all $c>0$, there exists a decreasing sequence $(\varphi_{c,l})_{l\geq 1}$ of functions converging to $\varphi$ such that:


•

$\varphi_{c,l}$ is smooth outside $X\backslash E_{c}$ ;



•

$dd^{c}\varphi_{c,l}+\alpha+A\|S\|\omega\geq 0$ where $A$ is a constant that depends only on $X$ and $\omega$;



•

for all $x\in X$, $\nu(\varphi_{c,l},x)=(\nu(\varphi,x)-c)_{+}:=\max(\nu(\varphi,x)-c,0)$.

results.title: A generalization of Nadel vanishing theorem
results.theorem:
Let $(X,\omega)$ be a complex manifold equipped with a Hermitian metric $\omega$, and $\Omega\Subset X$ be an open subset.
Assume that $T=\widetilde{T}+\frac{\mathrm{i}}{\pi}\partial\bar{\partial}\varphi$
is a closed $(1,1)$-current on $X$,
where $\widetilde{T}$ is a smooth real $(1,1)$-form and $\varphi$ is a quasi-plurisubharmonic function.
Let $\gamma$ be a continuous real $(1,1)$-form such that $T\geqslant\gamma$. Suppose that the Chern curvature tensor of $TX$ satisfies



$\left(\mathrm{i}\Theta_{T_{X}}+\theta\otimes\mathrm{Id}_{T_{X}}\right)\left(\kappa_{1}\otimes\kappa_{2},\kappa_{1}\otimes\kappa_{2}\right)\geqslant 0\quad\forall\kappa_{1},\kappa_{2}\in T_{X}~{}\text{with}~{}\langle\kappa_{1},\kappa_{2}\rangle=0$



for some continuous nonnegative $(1,1)$-form $\theta$ on $X$.
Then there is a family of closed $(1,1)$-currents $T_{\varsigma,\varepsilon}=\widetilde{T}+\frac{\mathrm{i}}{\pi}\partial\bar{\partial}\varphi_{\varsigma,\varepsilon}$ on $X$ such that


(i)

$\varphi_{\varsigma,\varepsilon}$ is quasi-plurisubharmonic on a neighborhood of $\bar{\Omega}$, smooth on $X\backslash E_{\sigma}(T)$, increasing with respect to $\varsigma$ and $\varepsilon$ on $\Omega$, and converges to $\varphi$ on $\Omega$ as $\varepsilon\to 0$,



(ii)

$T_{\varsigma,\varepsilon}\geqslant\gamma-\varsigma\theta-\delta_{\varepsilon}\omega$ on $\Omega$,



where $E_{\varsigma}(T)=\left\{x\in X;\nu(T,x)\geqslant\varsigma\right\}$, $\varsigma>0$, is the $\varsigma$-upperlevel set of Lelong numbers, and $\{\delta_{\varepsilon}\}$ is an increasing family of positive numbers such that $\lim_{\varepsilon\to 0}\delta_{\varepsilon}=0$.

results.title: Deformations of Kähler manifolds to normal bundles and restricted volumes of big classes
results.theorem:
Let $(X,\theta)$ be compact Kähler, $g$ a smooth function and $\psi$ a quasi-psh function with analytic singularities, and let $u$ be the corresponding envelope



$u:=\sup\{v\leq g-\psi:v\in PSH(X,\theta)\}.$



Then we have the Laplacian estimate



$0\leq n+\Delta_{\theta}u\leq((C+1)n+\sup_{X}(\Delta_{\theta}g))e^{B(g-\psi-\inf_{X}(g-\psi))},$



where $C$ is a constant such that $dd^{c}\psi\geq-C\theta$ and $-B$ is a negative lower bound of the holomorphic bisectional curvature of $\theta$.

kiselman.query: Kiselman minimum principle (partial Legendre transformation): If V is a complex domain, I is an open interval in R, and F is plurisubharmonic on V times {tau in C: Re tau in I} and independent of Im tau, then the function z -> inf_{s in I} F(z,s) is plurisubharmonic or identically minus infinity. Equivalently, for a rotation-invariant plurisubharmonic function on V times an annulus with logarithmically convex radial interval, its fiberwise infimum is plurisubharmonic. Apply with a finite locally bounded infimum after a smooth base quadratic correction.

results.title: Curvature strict positivity of direct image bundles associated to pseudoconvex families of domains
results.theorem:
Let $\Omega\subset U\times\mathbb{C}^{m}$ be a family of bounded domains over $U$ that admits a plurisubharmonic defining function,
and $\varphi$ be a $C^{2}$ plurisubharmonic function defined on some neighborhood of $\overline{\Omega}$ in $U\times\mathbb{C}^{m}$.
We assume that all fibers $\Omega_{t}\ (t\in U)$ are (connected) Reinhardt domains in $\mathbb{C}^{m}$ and $\varphi(t,z)$ is $T^{m}$- invariant with respect to $z$.
If $\varphi$ is strictly plurisubharmnic on some open subset $O$ in $\Omega$ such that $p(O)=U$,
then for any nonnegative integers $k_{1},\cdots,k_{m}$, the function $\psi(t)$ defined by



$e^{-\psi(t)}=\int_{\Omega_{t}}|z_{1}^{k_{1}}\cdots z_{m}^{k_{m}}|^{2}e^{-\varphi_{t}}d\lambda_{z}$



is a strictly plurisubharmonic function on $U$.

results.title: The Minimum Principle for Convex Subequations
results.theorem:
Let $X\subset\mathbb{C}^{n}$ be open and $F\subset J^{2,\mathbb{C}}(X)$ be a complex primitive subequation. Suppose



$f:\Omega^{\prime}\to\mathbb{R}$



is such that


(A)

$\Omega^{\prime}\subset X\times\mathbb{C}$ is open, $\mathbb{T}$-invariant and has connected fibres.



(C)

$f$ is $F\#_{\mathbb{C}}\mathcal{P}^{\mathbb{C}}$-subharmonic and $\mathbb{T}$-invariant.



(E)

$f$ attains is fibrewise minimum strictly in the interior.



(F)

$\Omega\subset X\times\mathbb{C}^{*}$.



(H)

$f$ is $\mathcal{C}^{2}$.



Then the marginal function



$g(z):=\inf_{w\in\Omega_{z}}f(z,w)\text{ for }z\in\pi(\Omega)$



is $F$-subharmonic.

results.title: Invariant Kähler potentials and symplectic reduction
results.theorem:
Let $B$ be a complexified $G$-orbit, $\rho$ a $G$-invariant strictly plurisubharmonic function and $p_{0}\in B$ a critical point of $\rho$. If
$\Sigma_{B}$ is a local submanifold transversal to the $G$-orbit $G\cdot p_{0}$ at $p_{0}$ of maximal dimension, then the restriction $\rho|_{\Sigma_{B}}$ has positive Hessian at $p_{0}$ and the $G$-orbit is a local isolated minimum locus
of $\rho$.

results.title: A simplified proof of optimal $L^2$-extension theorem and extensions from non-reduced subvarieties
results.theorem:
Let $f\in H^{0}(\Omega,\mathcal{I}(m_{p-1}\psi)/\mathcal{I}(m_{p}\psi))$. Assume that there exists a holomorphic function $F^{\circ}\in A^{2}(\Omega,\phi+m_{p-1}\psi)$ such that $F^{\circ}|_{\mathcal{O}/\mathcal{I}(m_{p}\psi)}=f$. Then the $L^{2}$-minimal extension $F_{0}\in A^{2}(\Omega,\phi+m_{p-1}\psi)$ of $f$ satisfies



$\int_{\Omega}|F_{0}|^{2}e^{-\phi-m_{p-1}\psi}\leq\limsup_{t\to-\infty}e^{-(m_{p}-m_{p-1})t}\int_{\Omega_{t}}|F^{\circ}|^{2}e^{-\phi-m_{p-1}\psi},$



where $\Omega_{t}:=\{\psi<t\}$.

results.title: Curvature strict positivity of direct image bundles associated to pseudoconvex families of domains
results.theorem:
Let $\Omega\subset U\times\mathbb{C}^{m}$ be a strictly pseudoconvex family of bounded domains over $U\subset\mathbb{C}^{n}$ and $\varphi$ be a $C^{2}$ plurisubharmonic function defined on some neighborhood of $\overline{\Omega}$ in $U\times\mathbb{C}^{m}$.
We assume that all fibers $\Omega_{t}\ (t\in U)$ are (connected) Reinhardt domains in $\mathbb{C}^{m}$ and $\varphi(t,z)$ is $T^{m}$- invariant with respect to $z$.
Then for any nonnegative integers $k_{1},\cdots,k_{m}$, the function $\psi(t)$ defined by



$e^{-\psi(t)}=\int_{\Omega_{t}}|z_{1}^{k_{1}}\cdots z_{m}^{k_{m}}|^{2}e^{-\varphi_{t}}d\lambda_{z}$



is a strictly plurisubharmonic function on $U$.

verification_report.summary: Correct under the accepted manuscript inputs. All sequential deductions pass, including the general Kiselman modulus, capped-minimum localization, freezing of nonclosed smooth forms, strict-barrier correction, and stability-to-continuity argument. [Demailly94, Theorem 4.1 and Remark 4.7](https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/regularization_flow.pdf) support the specialization to the closed current dd^c u with lower bound -theta. No power rate for epsilon or Holder exponent is inferred.
